implementedFoundation: tenant-scoped PostgreSQL Proposal, Draft, ApprovalEvent, ExecutionLease and timeline authorities exist
proposal and approval creation use transaction-scoped idempotency locks and exact proposal version and hash checks
maker cannot approve or execute its own proposal and an approver cannot execute the same proposal
approval quorum, proposal expiry, action-type snapshot drift, marking, field-write, kill and count guardrails are rechecked before lease
the canonical web SDK rereads authority after mutations and distinguishes approved, leased, applied and unknown states

findings.finding: create_proposal atomically creates both Proposal and a Draft already awaiting approval; there is no independently editable immutable Draft revision followed by an explicit submit-to-Proposal transition.
the risk classifier writes draftOnly=true for R1 and R4, but the approval service never enforces draftOnly; R1 can become approved and leased through the generic chain.
approval policy is a mutable keyword-classifier snapshot rather than an exact published RiskPolicy and ApprovalPolicy authority bound to W5-00 and W5-02.

approval eligibility is only a broad admin, approver or aip_approver role check; there is no assigned approver set, role-slot quorum, organization delegation, conflict-of-interest or policy-specific eligibility resolution.
approvalExpiresAt is caller optional and an approval without it remains valid indefinitely; no server policy constrains its TTL to Preview, account, adapter, budget reservation or proposal expiry.

ExecutionLease stores only proposalHash and owner; it does not persist or revalidate the W5-02 actionBindingHash, Preview, capability, account, adapter, RiskPolicy, BudgetPolicy, KillPolicy or dry-validation receipt.
lease acquisition increments a count-based budget unit but does not create an exact monetary or quota reservation that can be released on lease expiry and settled from UsageReceipt.

minimumApprovals counts distinct approving actor rows, but does not prove required role slots, ordered stages or independent business and compliance approvals; rejection and supersession semantics are not policy driven.

the generic authority supports a single hard-coded attempt and expiry check but no canonical expiry transition, renewal prohibition receipt, reservation release or explicit revocation event for a never-consumed lease.

the Draft Inbox displays approve, reject, lease and execute buttons by state only; backend roles fail closed, but the UI does not project user eligibility, required approval slots, binding drift or stable disabled reason codes before a mutation.
